stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking of major LLMs.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed improvement, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware for performance gains.
The feature is currently available in a preview build.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging apps.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is running AI tasks entirely on the user's own device.

stories.title: Big Tech accused of stonewalling European social media researchers
stories.author: Anna Desmarais, wired.com
bullet_points: Major tech platforms (TikTok, X, Meta) are accused of obstructing data access.
The obstruction involves failing to provide data that researchers claim is legally mandated.
The issue highlights ongoing regulatory and transparency challenges for Big Tech in Europe.

stories.title: CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference
stories.author: Vasilis Syrgkanis
bullet_points: Introduces CausalForge, a novel agentic framework designed to automate theoretical research specifically within causal inference.
Addresses a critical limitation in current LLM-based research loops: the empirical unreliability of LLMs as reviewers, which can accept fabricated results.
Grounds the framework in the Lean proof system to ensure formal correctness and self-improvement in the automated research process.

stories.title: CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference
stories.author: Vasilis Syrgkanis
bullet_points: Introduces CausalForge, a new framework designed for automated theoretical research in causal inference.
Addresses the critical issue of unreliable LLM reviewers, which often fail to accurately validate research findings.
Grounds the framework in the Lean proof system to ensure formal rigor and self-improvement in the research loop.

stories.title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
stories.author: Guanjun Jiang
bullet_points: The research addresses a core challenge in LLM self-evolution: balancing task diversity against reliable feedback.
Existing methods are limited; environment-bound approaches are narrow, while open-ended generation lacks reliable reward verification.
The paper proposes using 'agent skills' as a mechanism to push LLM capabilities through interaction-driven self-evolution.

stories.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
stories.author: Joaquim Pina
bullet_points: Investigates the non-transparent and unstable nature of how major LLMs (Claude, Grok, GPT, Gemini) validate contested scientific claims.
The study specifically tested LLM responses regarding ethnonationalist pseudo-science across different model families and time periods.
Highlights the critical issue of deployment configurations (e.g., API vs. web interface, specific model versions) influencing LLM output reliability.

stories.title: DBA-Bench: A Production-Fidelity Benchmark for LLM-Based Database Operations Agents
stories.author: Kai Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces DBA-Bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM-based database operations agents with production-level fidelity.
Highlights critical gaps in current LLM evaluation, specifically concerning live-environment interaction and complex observation spaces.
Addresses the need for benchmarks that account for solution-space openness, recognizing multiple operational trade-offs in remediation.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance the knowledge base and real-time data access of Claude Code.

stories.title: Apple is banking on privacy to set its smart glasses apart
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly planning to unveil its first smart glasses at WWDC next June.
The expected consumer launch window for these glasses is slated for the end of 2027.
Privacy features and messaging are cited as a key factor influencing Apple's development timeline.

stories.title: SpaceX eyes tower catch for next Starship after auspicious end to 13th flight
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX plans to attempt a tower catch for the next Starship flight.
This follows the successful conclusion of the 13th Starship flight.
The maneuver aims to recover the Starship vehicle near the launch pad.

stories.title: With help from data, art museums are reframing the visitor experience
stories.author: Mureji Fatunde-Iloeje
bullet_points: Art museums are integrating data analytics into their operations.
This data-driven approach is being used to redefine the visitor experience.
The trend reflects a broader shift in how cultural institutions are adopting technology.

stories.title: Anthropic's Opus 5 is about token efficiency, not a capability leap
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic's Opus 5 update is characterized by improvements in token efficiency rather than a massive leap in raw capability.
The article suggests that current, more cost-effective AI models are often sufficient for practical applications.
This signals a trend in the industry where optimization and efficiency are becoming as important as raw performance in LLMs.

stories.title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction
stories.author: Jiwen Lu
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of extending 3D reconstruction to 4D dynamic understanding using Geometry Foundation Models (GFMs).
Current motion perception methods often fail because they treat motion as independent point-wise displacements, ignoring physical structure.
The proposed SM4RT model aims to incorporate rigid-body kinematics, recognizing that real-world object motion is collective rather than isolated.

stories.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
stories.author: Salvatore Venticinque
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for Explainable Reinforcement Learning (XRL) in high-stakes environments.
Building trust in AI is identified as essential for advancing automation and human-AI collaboration in fields like aviation.
The research focuses on making AI decisions transparent to facilitate integration into critical systems like Air Traffic Control.

stories.title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents
stories.author: Baran Nama
bullet_points: The paper introduces the concept of 'The Regression Tax,' highlighting that adding skills to LLM agents can sometimes degrade performance.
The research moves beyond simple task success metrics by measuring both performance gains and performance losses (regressions).
The study validates these findings across extensive testing (6,000 runs) using multiple office automation benchmarks and model harness stacks.

stories.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
stories.author: Joaquim Pina
bullet_points: Investigates the lack of stability and transparency in how major LLMs (Claude, Grok, GPT, Gemini) validate contested scientific claims.
The study specifically tested LLMs' evaluation of ethnonationalist pseudo-science across different temporal snapshots.
Findings suggest that specific LLM deployment configurations (e.g., Grok's Fast versions) exhibit consistent biases in their responses.

stories.title: MineValiCoder: Reliable Code Generation with Test Case Quality Mining and Bipartite Graph-Based Mutual Validation
stories.author: Bo Li
bullet_points: Introduces MineValiCoder, a new method for reliable code generation using LLMs.
Addresses a key limitation in LLM-based TDD: the reliance on human-crafted test cases.
Mitigates issues arising from LLM stochasticity by employing test case quality mining and bipartite graph validation.

stories.title: Learning to Prepare Molecular Ground States with Transformer Models
stories.author: Enrico Rinaldi
bullet_points: The research addresses the computational bottleneck in quantum state preparation for large molecules.
It introduces ADAPT-GQE, a generative AI framework designed to synthesize efficient ground-state preparation circuits.
This work is highly relevant to advancing quantum chemistry and achieving practical quantum advantage in materials science and pharmaceuticals.

stories.title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
stories.author: Tushar Krishna
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of routing LLM calls in long-horizon, agentic AI workflows.
Identifies a limitation in existing routers: they make independent, per-call decisions, failing to account for delayed, task-level outcomes.
Proposes TRACE-ROUTER to enable task-consistent and adaptive routing based on overall workflow quality.

stories.title: PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest
stories.author: Zhihua Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces PinEqualizer, a system designed to solve the content cold-start problem in large-scale search and recommender systems.
The solution operates across the entire multi-stage content funnel, applicable to both search and recommendation surfaces.
It significantly reduces content bias, enabling more accurate model predictions across various content types.

stories.title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
stories.author: Casey R. Myers
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in Quantum Machine Learning (QML) where standard encoding units fail to capture matrix-level relationships.
It introduces a 'Quantum Spectral Model' designed to align the model's inductive bias with the spectral structure of matrix-valued inputs.
The core innovation involves explicitly constructing matrix-level representations using spectral values and subspaces, moving beyond simple coordinate-wise encoding.

stories.title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
stories.author: Zhandong Liu
bullet_points: Introduces 'bag-of-waves,' an interpretable framework for analyzing Electroencephalography (EEG) data.
Addresses limitations of traditional EEG analysis (predefined features) and deep learning (lack of interpretability, data hunger).
Aims to provide robust analysis in low-data regimes by learning a dictionary of recurring EEG waveforms.

stories.title: A Factorial Study of Synthetic Data Generation for Low-Resource Machine Translation using Grammar Books
stories.author: Rico Sennrich
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of low-resource machine translation for endangered languages lacking parallel data.
Proposes a novel pipeline using LLMs to extract linguistic data (rules, examples, lexicons) from existing grammar books.
Generates synthetic parallel corpora for fine-tuning, offering an improvement over prior methods that used grammar content only at inference time.

stories.title: Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation via Byte-Prefix Marginalization
stories.author: Honggang Qi
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of consolidating diverse, open-weight language models from different families.
It introduces Byte-Prefix Marginalization (BPM) to enable cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation (OPD).
BPM aims to overcome limitations in existing methods that discard teacher probability mass or misassign it across different tokenizers.

stories.title: Biomedical Machine Translation for Low-Resource Arabic-Script Languages via Cross-Lingual Transfer and LoRA Adapter Merging
stories.author: Lifeng Han
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of low-resource biomedical Natural Machine Translation (NMT) for Arabic-script languages.
Employs cross-lingual transfer, using Arabic and Persian as high-resource pivots to aid four low-resource targets (Dari, Pashto, Sorani Kurdish, Urdu).
Utilizes efficient fine-tuning techniques, specifically LoRA adapter merging, to improve translation quality.

stories.title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity
stories.author: Yingyue Luna Luan
bullet_points: The study investigates the alignment between Large Language Model (LLM) evaluations of creativity and human judgments.
Evidence regarding the convergence or divergence of LLM and human creativity assessments is currently mixed.
The research analyzed six popular LLMs across three studies to identify the underlying standards used by LLMs in creativity evaluation.

stories.title: From Isolated Tasks to Structured Capabilities: A Multilayer Taxonomy for Large Language Models
stories.author: Yanghua Xiao
bullet_points: The paper addresses the fragmentation in LLM evaluation, which is currently task-based rather than capability-based.
It introduces a novel, multi-layer taxonomy comprising 14 capability domains and 91 subskills.
The taxonomy is structured across Primitive, Constructed, and Integrative layers, guided by human cognitive science.

stories.title: Scriptc by Vercel: TypeScript-to-Native compiler, no JavaScript engine in binary
stories.author: maxloh
bullet_points: Scriptc is a new TypeScript-to-Native compiler developed by Vercel.
A key feature is that the resulting binary contains no JavaScript engine.
This suggests potential benefits in performance, size, or deployment environments.

stories.title: 🏢 Building Enterprise-Ready AI Agents 🤖 — A Practical Field Guide 📚
stories.author: truongpx396
bullet_points: Focuses on the practical aspects of building AI agents.
Covers the full lifecycle: design, shipping, and operation.
Addresses critical enterprise requirements like reliability, scalability, and performance.

stories.title: Permission-Aware RAG: Enforcing Document ACLs at Retrieval Time
stories.author: venkathub
bullet_points: Addresses a critical security gap in current Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) implementations.
Proposes 'Permission-Aware RAG' to enforce Access Control Lists (ACLs) during the retrieval phase.
Highlights the industry problem where most RAG demos lack any inherent security model.

stories.title: My AI agent tried to delete my secrets. It couldn't.
stories.author: julesrobineau
bullet_points: Discusses a practical DevSecOps approach to securing AI coding agents.
Proposes environment-specific scoping for AI agents (e.g., broad local access vs. read-only in production).
Highlights the importance of external guardrails and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for controlling agent behavior.
